doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Whether anything new excites him
summary: It is hard to hear anything new and what lasts just happens; he still goes back to older music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I agree too. Okay. That’s what I feel. I just wanted to know if you also felt that way.

I don’t feel – it’s hard to hear anything new, because it’s hard to try to do something new. I think if it’s something new that’s going to last, it just happens. I could be very well wrong at that. When you really try to – trying hard to make that go there, and then – then maybe it don’t last long. I don’t know.
Has any music that you’ve heard lately, that’s been produced, say, in the last ten years, that has gotten you excited?

Sure. I hear tunes by different people that I like. Some tunes, some part of tunes, but a group as a whole – I can’t think of no one group that I – I still like a lot of – I go back to a lot of the old stuff. I like some of the writing of the alto player – what’s his name? Played with the Messengers. I like some of his writing. He’s signed with CBS now [Bobby Watson]. You’ll think of it soon as you leave. Anyhow, it’s really not – I don’t know.
